# Installation

s1bursts needs a Python package, a free CDSE account, and ESA SNAP. Searching
the catalog works with the package alone; downloading needs the account, and
processing needs SNAP.

## Install the package

s1bursts requires Python 3.12 or newer and installs from PyPI:

::: {.panel-tabset group="installer"}

### pip

```{.bash}
pip install s1bursts
```

### uv

```{.bash}
uv add s1bursts
```

### pixi

```{.bash}
pixi add --pypi s1bursts
```

:::

## Install SNAP

Processing runs `gpt`, the command-line tool of SNAP version 13 or 14. Install
it with ESA's installer, or as a conda package:

::: {.panel-tabset group="snap"}

### ESA installer

Download [SNAP](https://step.esa.int/main/download/snap-download/) from ESA and
include the Microwave Toolbox, which holds the Sentinel-1 tools. The installer
does not always put `gpt` on your `PATH`; if it does not, set `SNAP_BIN` to the
installation's `bin` directory (see
[Environment variables](environment-variables.qmd)).

### conda or pixi

The [`esa-snap-s1tbx-gpt`](https://anaconda.org/channels/sarforge/packages/esa-snap-s1tbx-gpt/overview)
package installs `gpt` with the radar toolboxes and puts it on your `PATH`
whenever the environment is active. It is a community package, not published by
ESA, available for Linux, macOS and Windows.

```{.bash}
pixi workspace channel add sarforge
pixi add "esa-snap-s1tbx-gpt 14.*"
```

```{.bash}
conda install -c sarforge -c conda-forge "esa-snap-s1tbx-gpt=14"
```

:::

Use one SNAP version for one study. The versions give slightly different
results, so a time series that mixes them contains a small artificial step; see
[SNAP processing](snap-processing.qmd#snap-versions).

## Check that SNAP is found

s1bursts uses the `gpt` in `SNAP_BIN` if that is set, and otherwise the one on
your `PATH`. Check that your shell finds it:

```{.bash}
which gpt  # Linux and macOS
where gpt  # Windows
```

If this prints nothing and `SNAP_BIN` is not set, processing stops with a
`ConfigurationError`.

## Set up credentials

Downloads need a free [CDSE account](https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/).
s1bursts reads the account name and password from the environment variables
`CDSE_USERNAME` and `CDSE_PASSWORD`.
[Environment variables](environment-variables.qmd) shows how to set them and
lists the optional settings, including keys for a second download route.
